To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed and successfully tested a read-out buffer prototype, which is a functional and robust device, that meets the requirements for the read-out buffers of the ATLAS high level trigger system.
the read-out buffer prototype has been designed and built, that it can be integrated in a read-out-buffer complex and that it meets the performance requirements of the ATLAS trigger/DAQ system.
the performance of the prototype is sufficient to meet ATLAS specifications.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: - Design of a read-out buffers based on a custom PCI mezzanine.
the development of the hardware and the software that is needed to build a read-out buffer prototype that is suitable for the ATLAS trigger/DAQ system.
the design of a read-out system for the ATLAS High Level Trigger.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the performance of the read-out buffers is adequate to cope with ATLAS requirements, but that some improvements are needed to reach a higher level of robustness and reliability.
the prototype read-out buffer is a viable solution for the dataflow requirements of the ATLAS high level trigger.
we have demonstrated that the design is feasible and that the performance figures are in line with ATLAS requirements.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the prototype has proven the feasibility of the read-out buffer concept.
the prototype has been successfully tested in a real trigger scenario and that we have obtained a good understanding of the performance of the prototype and the limitations of the design.
the read-out buffers are ready for the ATLAS data taking.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the design of a read-out buffers is a complex task that needs to be addressed with care.
a custom made PCI card is a viable alternative to commercial boards in the context of a read-out complex.
the read-out buffers are ready for the installation in the ATLAS detector.
